correctness.rationale: Angular frequency n−1 survives the projection; integrating t=|z|² gives the unprojected squared norm (n+1)q_{n+1} and the sole projected coefficient squared n q_n² (zero for n=0). The residual cannot vanish: it is nonzero inside the disk and the multiplier vanishes outside, which no nonzero entire function can do. The factorial tail bounds every positive Schatten power at fixed T. With d_n=q_n(1−q_n), r_n=Pr(X=n+1), the exact identity is λ_n=q_n+n d_n−(n+1)r_n. On compact u windows the Poisson CLT and local mass bound give uniform λ_n/T→Φ(u)Φ(−u). Chernoff gives d_n≤C exp(−c(n−T)²/T) on [T/2,2T], exponential smallness on the left and geometric summability past 2T (the Poisson mass ratios are ≤1/2 there). This proves the tail sup bound and the level counts because all positive submaximal levels of the limit have measure-zero boundaries. It proves the stated Riemann sums, with q_n→1 uniformly below (1−δ)T and exponentially small beyond (1+δ)T. For p>1 the sharp upper bound is obtained by applying the coarse C_p bound only to the complement of the fixed A√T window: bulk is negligible and the rescaled edge tail is at most C_p times a Gaussian-tail integral tending to zero with A. For p<1 subadditivity and λ_n→1 on the strict bulk give both inequalities. At p=1 use a=√q_n, b=√(n d_n), c=√((n+1)r_n): the loss in replacing √(a²+b²−c²) by a+b is bounded by min(a,b)+c using √x−√(x−c²)≤c. In a relative δT window min(a,b)≤1 and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the c sum by √(2δT+O(1))√T; outside, both losses are o(T). This yields 1+I₁. I₂ is the mean positive part of an N(0,2) difference. Inspected CHECK.py by reading; its quadratures and truncated spectra are diagnostics, not what controls the infinite sums.
